note: Absolute budgets, deliberately loose: they exist to catch a large regression, not a 5% one.
Bytes are content, so they are machine-independent and can be tight. Timings are not, so their
headroom is ~3x (char) to ~5x (line) over the laptop they were set from: they trip at a ~4x
regression there. A machine N times slower multiplies its timing budgets by N
(KRD_BENCH_BUDGET_SCALE, 7.6 in CI) instead of these numbers being widened for everyone.
docs/BENCHMARK.md section 6 has the measurement, how to re-run it, and why a single absolute
number cannot also be a 2x gate on a 7.6x-slower runner.
